# The Great Advent Calendar Debate: Why Chocolate Still Reigns Supreme

The seasonal treat-based countdown might these days have expanded into cosmetics and booze, but nothing beats 24 days of chocolate. As November draws to a close and supermarket shelves groan under the weight of increasingly elaborate advent calendars, consumers face a dizzying array of choices that would have been unimaginable just a decade ago. From luxury skincare brands offering miniature serums behind each door to craft gin distilleries packaging 24 tiny bottles of botanical spirits, the advent calendar market has exploded into a multi-million-pound industry. Yet amid all this innovation and premiumisation, the humble chocolate advent calendar remains the undisputed champion of the Christmas countdown, holding a special place in the hearts of children and adults alike.

***

The transformation of the advent calendar from a simple religious tradition into a commercial phenomenon has been nothing short of remarkable. What began in 19th-century Germany as a way to mark the days of Advent with prayers and Bible verses gradually evolved through the 20th century into the cardboard-and-chocolate format most of us grew up with. The thrill of punching open a tiny perforated window each morning, revealing a misshapen star or lopsided Christmas tree made of waxy milk chocolate, became one of the defining rituals of a British childhood. It didn't matter that the chocolate was often mediocre at best — the magic lay in the daily anticipation, the sense of time slowly unwinding toward the big day.

***

In recent years, however, the advent calendar has undergone a dramatic reinvention. High-end beauty brands such as Charlotte Tilbury, Jo Malone, and Dior now offer calendars costing upwards of £150, filled with sample-sized products that promise to pamper their owners through the darkest weeks of winter. Alcohol companies have joined the fray with enthusiasm, offering everything from whisky and wine to craft beer and artisan gin. There are advent calendars for cheese lovers, hot sauce enthusiasts, candle collectors, and even dog owners who want their pets to share in the festive fun. The trend has become so pervasive that it sometimes feels as though every conceivable product category has been squeezed into the format, regardless of whether it truly belongs there.

***

But for all their Instagram-friendly appeal, these luxury alternatives often miss the fundamental point of what makes an advent calendar special. The beauty calendar, once opened, becomes just another collection of half-used products cluttering a bathroom shelf. The gin calendar, however elegantly packaged, is essentially just an expensive way to buy miniatures. They cater to adult desires for novelty and indulgence, but they lack the innocent, almost sacred quality of the childhood chocolate calendar — that sense of a small, daily miracle unfolding behind each numbered door. There is something profoundly satisfying about the simplicity of the original concept: one day, one door, one small piece of chocolate, one step closer to Christmas morning.

***

This year, the chocolate advent calendar market itself has evolved to offer something for every taste and budget. Supermarkets stock reliable favourites from Cadbury and Mars alongside increasingly sophisticated options from artisan chocolatiers who fill their calendars with single-origin truffles and hand-painted bonbons. Whether you spend £1.50 on a basic Dairy Milk calendar or £50 on a handcrafted selection from a boutique chocolate maker, the essential experience remains the same — and it remains magical. So while the rest of the advent calendar world continues its relentless expansion into ever more unlikely territories, there is comfort in knowing that the original and best version endures. After all, Christmas is ultimately about tradition, anticipation, and small moments of sweetness shared with the people we love. And for that, nothing beats chocolate.
